author: bd-spin/bd-spin-20260511T212242Z-1478141
text:
Diagnosis 2026-05-11 by do-beads loop: tc60 is NOT a path-builder bug; it is a harness/API-gap issue. Details:

Pool topology: 6 intermediates form a small cross-signed graph with subjects {A, B, C} and the anchor. Each of A, B, C has two intermediate forms — one issued upstream by the next letter, one issued by anchor. Two of the six intermediates (int-00 B-from-C, int-05 A-from-anchor) use signature algorithm ecdsa-with-SHA1 (OID 1.2.840.10045.4.1, LEGACY). The other four use ecdsa-with-SHA256.

build_path correctly enumerates 4 candidate chains via build_path_candidates. The first returned candidate is [peer, int-00 (SHA-1), int-03, int-05 (SHA-1)] — DFS-order, length 4. validate_path then rejects on SignatureInvalid{index:3} because DefaultVerifier does not dispatch ecdsa-with-SHA1 (project policy: SHA-1 ECDSA excluded).

There IS a valid SHA-256-only path in the pool: [peer, int-01 (B-from-A), int-02 (A-from-C), int-04 (C-from-anchor)]. All four use ecdsa-with-SHA256. openssl + pyca pick exactly this path.

The genuine issue: build_path is a single-shot wrapper that returns only the first candidate from build_path_candidates. It has no SignatureVerifier dependency, so it cannot know in advance which candidates will fail validate_path. The consumer pattern (limbo loader, PKITS loader, the user's main loop) is expected to either:
  (a) iterate build_path_candidates and find the first chain whose validate_path returns Ok, OR
  (b) accept the first candidate and treat validate_path failure as terminal.

pkix-difftest's limbo/PKITS loaders today follow pattern (b) — they call build_path and feed the single chain to validate_path. That is the actual gap that surfaces tc60.

Options for the fix:
  1. Harness change in pkix-difftest: in the limbo loader (and possibly PKITS), iterate build_path_candidates and try each via validate_path until one passes or the iterator is exhausted. Minimal scope; mirrors PKIX-t0w4's PKITS-side change. Re-runs eliminate tc60 from StricterThanWild.
  2. New helper in pkix-path-builder: pub fn build_first_valid_path<V>(target, pool, anchors, policy, verifier) -> Result<Vec<Certificate>>. Combines candidates + validate_path into one call. Useful API addition for downstream consumers facing adversarial pools.
  3. Promote build_path to iterate candidates internally if it accepts a verifier. API-breaking change to the most-used surface.

Recommendation: ship option 1 (harness fix) — minimal scope, matches the existing PKITS-side pattern. Option 2 is a useful follow-up API addition but not required to close tc60 in the corpus. Option 3 is rejected (breaking change to a frequently-called API for a corner case).

Rescoping the bead away from 'path-builder bug at depth 3' to 'limbo harness must iterate build_path_candidates when validate_path fails on the first chain' is the honest framing. The bead title 'pkix-path-builder: fix bettertls::pathbuilding::tc60 intermediate selection at depth 3' is wrong about both location (pkix-difftest harness, not pkix-path-builder) and mechanism (signature-algorithm filter, not intermediate selection).

Releasing the claim back to open so a focused future session can decide between option 1 and option 2 with explicit authorization. Adding 'human' label because the choice of architecture (helper in pkix-path-builder vs harness fix in pkix-difftest) is a design call benefiting from explicit confirmation.
